title: Circuit Breaker Sandbox: Vesting Contracts vs Price Caps
paper: 2602.12782 Dual-Defense Mechanism, Singapore electricity market

discussion_why: fits gambling/exchange mechanics directly -- feels like tuning a sportsbook's max-bet and in-play suspension rules and watching line volatility change

title: Why Sportsbooks (and Power Grids) Both Need Circuit Breakers
paper: 2602.12782 Dual-Defense Mechanism, Singapore electricity market
pitch: Explainer comparing Singapore's vesting-contract + temporary-price-cap combo to sportsbook bet limits, exchange trading halts, and Polymarket's liquidity mechanisms -- same 'decouple price suppression from liquidity risk' problem everywhere prices clear under panic.
discussion_why: wins on debate -- bettors love arguing about whether limits/halts protect the market or just protect the house

title: Same-Game Parlay Blind-Spot Simulator
paper: 2602.12023 Decomposition of Spillover Effects Under Misspecification
pitch: Single-file toy: set a 'true' correlation structure between two same-game parlay legs (e.g., QB yards and team total, mixing a real network channel and a real market-wide channel), then pick a deliberately wrong summary statistic a bettor/model might use, and watch the demo show the estimated 'spillover' still gets the direction right but the magnitude wrong -- visualizes the paper's pseudo-true estimand result live.
discussion_why: wins on relatability -- everyone on a betting Discord has an opinion about whether their parlay-correlation model is 'basically right' or garbage

title: Your Correlation Model Is Wrong But Still Useful (Here's the Math)
paper: 2602.12023 Decomposition of Spillover Effects Under Misspecification
pitch: Explainer on why a misspecified 'share of treated neighbors' spillover proxy (from cash-transfer econ) still recovers the sign of network effects -- reframed via fantasy football 'teammate effect' stats and same-game parlay correlation assumptions.
discussion_why: wins on surprise -- 'your wrong model still points the right way' is a satisfying gotcha for stats-curious bettors

title: Mode-Blind BERT: The Hidden Bimodal Range Toy
paper: 2608.01383 An Identifiability Theory of Masked Prediction
pitch: Single-file HTML toy: a 2D bimodal distribution (e.g., a poker opponent's hand-strength range with two clusters -- 'bluff' and 'value') is fed through a tiny masked-prediction game where you tune the mask visibility slider; the demo shows loss staying near-zero while the recovered mixture weights (bluff % vs value %) drift wildly, visually proving 'low loss does not mean you learned the true distribution.'
discussion_why: wins on surprise -- 'your model can ace its loss function and still have no idea about the actual bluff/value split' is a great poker-nerd gut-punch

title: Range-Reveal Mask Schedule Checker
paper: 2608.01383 An Identifiability Theory of Masked Prediction
pitch: Small local tool applying the paper's identifiability-modulus math to a toy poker-range-prediction model: given a masking schedule for training data (which betting-round info gets hidden), estimate whether it's 'mode-blind' to rare hand types (like slowplayed monsters) before you bother training the real model.
discussion_why: fits AI+poker crossover, appeals to Discord members building their own solver/range tools

title: Mode Blindness: Why Masked-Model AI Confidently Misses Rare Events
paper: 2608.01383 An Identifiability Theory of Masked Prediction
pitch: Explainer using dice/roulette mixture analogies (e.g., a rigged die that's secretly two dice mixed) to show why masked prediction (BERT/MAE-style) training can achieve near-zero loss while getting the mixture weights of rare outcomes badly wrong.
discussion_why: wins on whimsy -- the rigged-dice framing turns dense ML theory into a casino magic trick

title: Bandit Bias Live: Watch UCB1 Lie to You
paper: 2608.01069 Characterizing Bias in Post-Bandit Inference under Index Algorithms
pitch: Single-file HTML/canvas casino-style demo: a bank of slot machines (bandit arms) with hidden true win rates gets auto-played by UCB1 in real time; two live counters show the 'naive sample-mean' win rate per arm vs the true win rate, and the gap visibly refuses to close (matching the paper's 1/sqrt(log T) decay) even after thousands of pulls. Add a slider for exploration constant to show the regret-bias tradeoff directly.
discussion_why: wins on surprise -- 'the AI picking your bets is systematically fooling itself about how good each bet is, and barely gets better with more data' is a killer hook for a betting/AI Discord

title: Bandit Backtest Bias Auditor
paper: 2608.01069 Characterizing Bias in Post-Bandit Inference under Index Algorithms
pitch: Diagnostic script for any adaptive bet-sizing / DFS lineup bot that uses a UCB-style index to allocate stakes across strategies: computes the paper's 'effective exploration rate' from the bot's actual pull history and reports how biased its self-reported win rates for underexplored arms likely are, before anyone trusts the backtest.
discussion_why: fits decision-theory + betting directly, and stings anyone on the server who's been bragging about a bandit-optimized bot's backtested edge

title: The Bandit Trap: Why 'Worse' Casino Arms Might Secretly Be Tied
paper: 2608.01069 Characterizing Bias in Post-Bandit Inference under Index Algorithms
pitch: Explainer on the regret-bias tradeoff in UCB1-style algorithms: more exploration cuts inference bias but costs you real money/regret, framed as a betting-bankroll decision (do you want a bot that learns fast and lies to you, or learns slow and tells the truth?).
discussion_why: wins on fit with decision-theory/gambling -- directly the 'explore vs exploit with your own money' debate

title: Metabolic Tilt Simulator
paper: 2602.13421 Metabolic cost of information processing in Poisson variational autoencoders
pitch: Single-page toy that models a poker player as a Poisson-VAE-style spiking system with a fixed 'metabolic budget': as a session slider drains the budget, decision-quality (bet sizing, bluff-catching accuracy) visibly degrades, mirroring the paper's finding that KL-cost forces sparser, cheaper coding as the penalty rises. Frame it explicitly as 'this is what tilt looks like as an information-theoretic energy crisis.'
discussion_why: Directly on-brand for a poker/decision-theory Discord: it turns 'why do I play worse late in a session' into a testable, gambling-flavored claim, and the neuroscience hook ('your brain literally budgets calories for decisions') is a strong wait-really surprise.

title: Brain Battery: interactive Poisson-VAE sparsity dial
paper: 2602.13421 Metabolic cost of information processing in Poisson variational autoencoders
pitch: A canvas toy visualizing spike trains encoding a simple image/pattern, with a slider for the KL-weight coefficient; dragging it shows spikes thinning out and reconstruction getting blockier in real time, illustrating the paper's core tradeoff (sparsity vs. fidelity) without needing to actually train anything.
discussion_why: Cool neuroscience-viz but mostly appeals to ai/bio nerds rather than sparking betting/games debate.

title: Why Thinking Burns Calories (and Why You Tilt at 2am)
paper: 2602.13421 Metabolic cost of information processing in Poisson variational autoencoders
pitch: Explainer connecting the P-VAE's emergent 'metabolic cost term' to real decision fatigue in poker/trading — biology of why late-session decisions get sparser and worse, using the paper's sparsity-vs-KL-weight result as the hook.
discussion_why: Good relatability hook for anyone who's played a long session, but it's a video essay, not something to argue over live.

title: Draw the Power Law
paper: 2603.03337 Does the motor cortex draw on a wire plane?

Directly demos the phenomenon the paper's geometry paper is explaining.
discussion_why: Strong wait-really surprise (your hand physically can't violate a math law) but limited betting/sports crossover unless framed as a game.

title: Power Law Sports Bet: whose mechanics are more 'optimal'?
paper: 2603.03337 Does the motor cortex draw on a wire plane?

title: The Motor Cortex Doesn't Draw on Paper — It Draws on a Wire
paper: 2603.03337 Does the motor cortex draw on a wire plane?

discussion_why: Niche differential-geometry-meets-neuroscience content; cool for math nerds but a harder sell for general discussion.
